title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Swagger UI Plugin via request path
analysis:
The Ktor Swagger UI plugin dynamically generates HTML containing a Javascript block that incorporates `call.request.path()` (which corresponds to `fullPath`) into a string literal. Since `fullPath` is extracted directly from the HTTP request line without any sanitization or encoding, an attacker can supply a specially crafted request path containing single quotes to escape the Javascript string delimiter and inject arbitrary executable Javascript payload (XSS).

### Conceptual Exploit Payload
If the Swagger UI is mapped to `/swagger`, an attacker can craft a request such as:
`GET /swagger',x:alert(document.domain),y:' HTTP/1.1`

The server will generate the following HTML and Javascript block:
```html
<script>
window.onload = function() {
    window.ui = SwaggerUIBundle({
        url: '/swagger',x:alert(document.domain),y:'/documentation.yaml',
        dom_id: '#swagger-ui',
...
```
This is valid Javascript syntax that will immediately execute the injected `alert(document.domain)` function in the victim's browser when they access the URL.
